Closes #2617

coupling: Stack buffer overflow in knownhost_line_legacy() reached via libssh2_knownhost_readline(). The two commits each look correct in isolation and the bug exists only in their composition. Commit a23f946 ('knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals', which reworks plain-hostname matching) de-tracks the legacy plain-hostname length guard from the stack buffer it protects: 'if(namelen >= sizeof(hostbuf) - 1)' becomes 'if(namelen > 254)'. That is behavior-identical while hostbuf stays 256 bytes, so the diff is benign on its own. Commit 8b2c24b ('tidy-up: miscellaneous') then shrinks the scratch buffer to the DNS limit: 'char hostbuf[256]' becomes 'char hostbuf[254]'. With the original sizeof-based guard this is also safe (the guard auto-tracks and caps names at 252), so its diff is benign on its own as well. Only with BOTH commits can a single 254-char hostname pass the now hard-coded 'namelen > 254' check, after which 'memcpy(hostbuf, name, 254); hostbuf[254] = '\0';' writes one byte past the end of hostbuf[254]. A correct fix is non-local: restoring only the sizeof-tracked guard protects the shrunk buffer, and restoring only the 256-byte buffer makes the hard-coded 254 limit fit again; reasoning about either single diff alone cannot reveal the overflow.
